wph37f: This week you review two classes: the imperfect, to describe and tell past habits, and how it combines with the simple past to tell a complete anecdote. Here you see it with other examples and an image that helps you choose.
10lhg5a: The forms: -aba, -ía and only three irregular verbs
mbwrkk: The imperfect is the most regular tense in Spanish. Verbs in **-ar** take **-aba** (_cantaba_); verbs in **-er** and **-ir** take **-ía** (_comía_, _vivía_). The yo and él forms are the same: the context or the pronoun shows who it is.
xobffp: Watch the accents: **nosotros** with -ar has one (_cantábamos_) and all the -ía forms have one (_comíamos_, _vivían_).
1g9yqp3: There are only three irregular verbs: **ser** (_era_), **ir** (_iba_) and **ver** (_veía_). Everything else is regular, including _tener_, _hacer_ and _poder_: _tenía_, _hacía_, _podía_.
16pp8ez: The imperfect of _ir_ is spelled with **b**: **iba**.
1l8ze7s: What it's for: describing, habits and actions in progress
qo75bq: **Describing** people, places and situations in the past: _La casa era blanca y tenía un patio con plantas._ Also the time, age and weather: _Eran las seis_, _Tenía diez años_, _Hacía calor_.
1etpv2j: **Telling habits**: what normally happened, many times. Markers: **antes**, **de niño**, **cuando era pequeña**, **siempre**, **todos los domingos**, **a menudo**. _Todos los veranos íbamos al lago._
14j1f8l: **Presenting an action in progress**: something was happening at a moment in the past, without saying when it ended. _A las ocho yo cenaba y mi hermana estudiaba._
10f12z5: If in English you can say _used to_ or _was …-ing_, in Spanish it's almost always the imperfect.
1qmv00m: Age and stage of life are description: **era** pequeño.
1u26npv: **Todos los días** and **antes** mark a habit: imperfect.
y16y0z: Scene and events: imperfect and simple past together
1v3h3x6: Imagine a play. The **imperfect** paints the **set**: where we were, what the weather was like, what was going on. The **simple past** tells the **events** that move the story forward: what happened, what each person did.
1tyegru: That's why an anecdote often starts in the imperfect and switches to the simple past with **de repente**, **entonces** or **en ese momento**: _Llovía y todos dormían. De repente, alguien llamó a la puerta._
9rse9c: **Cuando** doesn't decide the tense: look at what happens. _Cuando llegué, mi madre cocinaba_ (my mother's action was in progress). _Cuando llegué, mi madre cocinó_ (first I arrived, then she started cooking).
182o8n7: Everyone was already asleep when I came in: an action in progress, **dormían**.
179ghiv: **Había** describes what existed in the scene: _Había mucha gente en la plaza_. **Hubo** presents something that **happened**: _Hubo una tormenta_, _Hubo un accidente_, _Hubo una fiesta_.
yrvr5u: **Era** describes: _Era un día gris_. **Fue** evaluates a complete, finished event: _El concierto fue increíble_. If you're talking about a specific event, don't use _era_: say _hubo_ or _fue_.
y1iftz: Both forms of _haber_ have no plural in this use: _había dos coches_, _hubo tres conciertos_, never _habían dos coches_.
304ai1: A specific event is introduced with **hubo**.
xz0hq3: _Haber_ with this meaning has no plural: **había**.

1ni42r0: The stressed í of había, tenía, vivía
gbqof8: In **-ía** forms, the **i** is stressed and separates from the next vowel: _te-NÍ-a_, _vi-VÍ-a_, _ha-BÍ-a_. That's **three** syllables, not two. If you say _te-NIA_ in two syllables, it sounds odd or isn't understood.
5hk24o: The same happens with _comíamos_ (co-MÍ-a-mos) and _veían_ (ve-Í-an). The accent on the í reminds you where your voice goes.
15zpfbu: Compare with words where the i isn't stressed: _FE-ria_ in two syllables versus _te-NÍ-a_ in three, or _jun-TA-ba_, where the stress is on the a. In the -aba imperfect the stress never falls at the end: _ju-GA-ba_, _ju-GÁ-ba-mos_.
12c64u2: The -ía forms always have an accent (_tenía_, _vivían_) because the í separates from the a. The -aba forms only have one with nosotros: _jugábamos_.
swijw5: _de-CÍ-a_ with a clear í; _E-ra_ stressed at the start.
1f0bacw: In -ábamos the stress is on the **á**: _ju-GÁ-ba-mos_.
